rule: Working branch never tracks trunk, and the first PR push sets the branch's own upstream
description: `plugin/skills/create-working-branch/SKILL.md` requirement 6 is the source for the rule that a newly created working branch carries no upstream: it is created from `base` with `git switch --no-track -c`, because creating it from a remote-tracking base such as `origin/main` would otherwise make it track trunk, letting a plain `git push` or a force-with-lease retry against the tracked upstream target trunk. The source pin is ONE span carrying both the condition (the working branch does NOT yet exist) and the obligation (create it from `base` via `git switch --no-track -c <working_branch> <base>`); dropping `--no-track` or rewriting either half turns the suite red. Nine consumers keep the rule closed at its other points. In the same file, the existing-branch path must still carry the clause that, after `git switch <working_branch>`, an upstream whose name is not `<remote>/<working_branch>` is removed with `git branch --unset-upstream`; that pin spans both the mismatch condition and the unset obligation. Every push of the working branch runs through `plugin/skills/push-branch/scripts/push-branch.sh`, and six pins in that script carry the push-side clauses. The mode-selection span carries the explicit mode taken when `--remote` is given, the read of `branch.<b>.remote` and `branch.<b>.merge` for the current branch, the condition that either is set, and the guard that stops with the exact blocker `upstream does not match the working branch` when either is empty, when the merge ref is not `refs/heads/$current_branch`, or when the upstream remote fails the identifier gate, before upstream mode is selected. The origin-mode span carries the condition (no upstream, `--no-upstream origin`, and `remote.origin.url` set), the obligation (push to `origin` in origin mode), the deferral with a warning when `remote.origin.url` is unset, and the block when no upstream and no remote is supplied. The push span carries the single push of the refspec `${head_sha}^{commit}:refs/heads/$current_branch`, with no `-u` in any mode: the source is the captured commit by object id in peel form, which no refname can shadow because no refname can contain `^`, and the destination is the branch's own name. The upstream-record span carries the explicit upstream record: after a successful push in any mode other than upstream (that is, explicit and origin modes), the script itself writes `branch.$current_branch.remote` as the push remote and `branch.$current_branch.merge` as `refs/heads/$current_branch`, because `-u` records nothing for an object-id source, so the explicit and origin first pushes set an upstream named after the branch itself. The retry span carries the force-with-lease retry of a non-fast-forward, taken in upstream mode only, against the same push remote and the same object-id refspec. The `run_git_push` span carries the single `git push --porcelain` that every push and retry runs. Rewriting the comparison target, the blocker, the mode conditions, the refspec source or destination, adding `-u` to the push, dropping or reconditioning the upstream record or retargeting either of its writes, or retargeting the retry, turns the suite red. Two consumers pin the skill prose that selects the modes, each as the script invocation with its mode flags: `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/SKILL.md` step 6 passes `--no-upstream origin`, so a branch with no upstream makes its first push to `origin`; `plugin/skills/push-branch/SKILL.md` requirement 2 passes `--no-upstream block`, so a remediation push with no upstream blocks rather than choosing a remote. Changing either flag, or replacing either invocation with a direct push, turns the suite red. The script's behavior, including that a mismatched upstream blocks before any push that every push and retry writes only the branch's own ref, that the commit written is the captured one even when the branch ref is rewritten or a ref named after the commit exists, and that a failed upstream write blocks after the push, is additionally asserted by `tools/test_push_branch.sh`. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these ten word sequences exist in these four named files; they claim nothing about meaning. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) the fenced Bash block that implements the unset-upstream comparison in create-working-branch is NOT pinned, so a rewrite of that block that no longer compares against `refs/remotes/$rem/$b` stays green while the prose clause survives; (2) the script lines between the pinned spans, including the upstream-mode push remote resolution (`branch.<b>.pushRemote`, then `remote.pushDefault`, then the upstream remote), the refusal of the `.` remote, the classification of the push result, and the `write_config_value` helper body with its blocker, are outside these pins and rest on `tools/test_push_branch.sh`; (3) the open-plan-pr handling of a `warning:` line (record it and continue to step 7) is outside the pinned spans; (4) a meaning inversion around the pinned bytes, such as surrounding prose that makes the unset or the script optional, or script code added between the spans that rewrites a captured value, is invisible; (5) the pins see only the four files they name, and no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW branch-creating or branch-pushing skill that never carries these clauses, which is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.

source.pattern: if `working_branch` does NOT yet exist, create it from `base` via `git switch --no-track -c <working_branch> <base>`

consumers.pattern: After `git switch <working_branch>`, if an upstream is set and its name is not `<remote>/<working_branch>`, run `git branch --unset-upstream`.

if [ "$remote_seen" = true ]; then push_mode='explicit' push_remote="$remote_name" else read_config_value "branch.$current_branch.remote" upstream_remote="$config_value" read_config_value "branch.$current_branch.merge" upstream_merge="$config_value" if [ -n "$upstream_remote" ] || [ -n "$upstream_merge" ]; then [ -n "$upstream_remote" ] && [ -n "$upstream_merge" ] || blocker "upstream does not match the working branch" [ "$upstream_merge" = "refs/heads/$current_branch" ] || blocker "upstream does not match the working branch" hivemind_assert_identifier "$upstream_remote" || blocker "upstream does not match the working branch" push_mode='upstream'

elif [ "$no_upstream" = 'origin' ]; then read_config_value "remote.origin.url" if [ -z "$config_value" ]; then printf 'branch: %s
commit: %s
warning: %s
' "$current_branch" "$head_sha" \ "no upstream and no origin remote; push deferred" exit 0 fi push_mode='origin' push_remote='origin' else blocker "no upstream and no remote supplied" fi
